evidence.text: od which has been subjected to sorting or other physical treatment to reduce contamination levels may be placed on the market provided that the maximum levels set out in Annex I for food placed on the market for the final consumer or use as a food ingredient are not exceeded and that the treatment used has not resulted in the presence of other harmful residues.

evidence.location: Article 5 — Food to be subjected to sorting or other physical treatment before placing on the market for the final consumer or use as a food ingredient
evidence.text: Article 5 Food to be subjected to sorting or other physical treatment before placing on the market for the final consumer or use as a food ingredient 1. Where a maximum level for a contaminant is set out in Annex I specifically as regards food to be subjected to sorting or other physical treatment before placing on the market for the final consumer or use as a food ingredient, such food may be placed on the market provided that: (a) it is not placed on the market for the final consumer or use as a food ingredient; (b) it complies with the maximum level set out in Annex I for that contaminant in that food to be subjected to sorting or other physical treatment before placing on the market for the final consumer or use as a food ingredient; and (c) it is labelled and marked in accordance with paragraph 2. 2. The label of each individual package and the original accompanying document of food referred to in paragraph 1, point (c), shall clearly show its use and bear the following information: ‘Product shall be subjected to sorting or other physical treatment to reduce [name contaminant(s)] contamination before placing on the market for the final consumer or use as a food ingredient’. The consignment/batch identification code shall be indelibly marked on each individual package of the consignment and on the original accompanying document. 3. Food to be subjected to sorting or other physical treatment to reduce contamination levels shall not prior to this be mixed with food placed on the market for the final consumer or with food intended for use as a food ingredient. 4. final_output:
## 1. Short assessment

**The supplied snapshot does not show a different aflatoxin limit for dried figs simply because they are intended for sorting or other physical treatment.** It lists the dried-fig maximum levels as **6.0 μg/kg for aflatoxin B1 and 10.0 μg/kg for the sum of aflatoxins**. The dried-fig entry does not specify a separate sorting-treatment category. [E84bba6f619]

These are snapshot values, not confirmation of the law effective on the relevant date.

## 2. Evidence-supported law

The supplied row reads: **“Dried figs | 6,0 | 10,0”** under the aflatoxin B1 and sum-of-aflatoxins columns. [E84bba6f619]

Article 5’s sorting/physical-treatment conditions apply where Annex I **specifically** sets a maximum level for food in that category. The supplied dried-fig row does not identify such a separate category, so the evidence does not support applying a different limit to these figs merely because sorting is intended. [E908c5eea55] The separate sorting-treatment entry cited in the snapshot is for tree nuts, not dried figs. [E0f3287ac2b]

## 3. Facts/currentness to verify

The measured concentration, intended use, and any supporting shipment evidence are not provided. A detection alone does not establish that either listed maximum level is exceeded.

The supplied snapshot does not establish that these limits or the relevant Article 5 text are effective for the legally relevant date. [E84bba6f619] [E908c5eea55]

## 4. Practical next checks

- Confirm the analytical result for aflatoxin B1 and, where relevant, the sum of aflatoxins, then compare it with the applicable limit.
- Confirm whether the consignment is intended for direct consumer use, as a food ingredient, or for sorting/physical treatment.
- Verify the applicable official EU text and amendments for the relevant date.

**CRITICAL uncovered issues**
- **Current-law gap:** effective status of the dried-fig limit and Article 5 text is unverified.
- **Case-fact gap:** the consignment’s intended use and supporting evidence are not provided.
